```{python}
#| label: prepare-report
#| include: false

from datetime import datetime, timedelta, timezone
from importlib.metadata import version as package_version
from pathlib import Path
import platform

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import matplotlib.dates as mdates
from matplotlib.lines import Line2D
from matplotlib.patches import Patch
import pandas as pd
from IPython.display import Markdown, display

from mmc_watershed_data.geospatial import (
    load_station_points,
    load_watershed_boundary,
)
from mmc_watershed_data.reporting import load_report_dataset
from mmc_watershed_data.stations import AUBURN_STATIONS, OPELIKA_STATIONS


def find_project_root(start: Path) -> Path:
    """Find the repository root from Quarto's execution directory."""

    for candidate in (start, *start.parents):
        if (candidate / "pyproject.toml").is_file():
            return candidate
    raise RuntimeError("Could not locate the MMC project root.")


project_root = find_project_root(Path.cwd().resolve())
dataset = load_report_dataset(project_root)

frame = pd.DataFrame(
    [
        {
            "city": record.city,
            "station_key": record.station_key,
            "station_name": record.station_name,
            "timestamp": record.timestamp,
            "rain_in": record.rain_in,
        }
        for record in dataset.records
    ]
)
station_summary = (
    frame.groupby(["city", "station_name"], as_index=False)
    .agg(
        total_rain_in=("rain_in", "sum"),
        observations=("rain_in", "size"),
        wet_observations=("rain_in", lambda values: int((values > 0).sum())),
        maximum_interval_rain_in=("rain_in", "max"),
    )
    .sort_values(["total_rain_in", "station_name"], ascending=[False, True])
)
time_series_frame = frame.sort_values(
    ["city", "station_name", "timestamp"]
).reset_index(drop=True)
winner = station_summary.iloc[0]
period_label = (
    f"{dataset.start_date:%B %d, %Y} through {dataset.end_date:%B %d, %Y}"
)
total_rainfall = float(station_summary["total_rain_in"].sum())
winner_share = (
    float(winner["total_rain_in"]) / total_rainfall if total_rainfall > 0 else 0.0
)
city_totals = station_summary.groupby("city")["total_rain_in"].sum().to_dict()
configured_station_names = {
    station.name for station in AUBURN_STATIONS + OPELIKA_STATIONS
}
represented_station_names = set(station_summary["station_name"])
missing_station_names = sorted(configured_station_names - represented_station_names)
coverage_sentence = (
    "All configured stations are represented."
    if not missing_station_names
    else "No processed observations were available for "
    + ", ".join(missing_station_names)
    + "."
)
rendered_at = datetime.now(timezone.utc).replace(microsecond=0)
station_points = load_station_points(project_root)
watershed_boundary = load_watershed_boundary(project_root)
chart_start = pd.Timestamp(dataset.start_date)
chart_end = pd.Timestamp(dataset.end_date + timedelta(days=1))

report_metadata = pd.DataFrame(
    [
        ("Selected input", dataset.selection),
        ("Requested period", f"{dataset.start_date} through {dataset.end_date}"),
        ("Processed station files", len(dataset.source_files)),
        ("Validated observations", len(dataset.records)),
        ("Stations represented", len(station_summary)),
        ("Rainfall unit", "inches per processed interval"),
        (
            "Auburn source",
            "https://www.licor.cloud/api/v2/timeseriesdata",
        ),
        (
            "Opelika source",
            "https://360.thormobile.net/thorcloud/api/weatherpacketsbyinterval",
        ),
        ("Project version", package_version("mmc-watershed-data")),
        ("Python", platform.python_version()),
        ("Rendered (UTC)", rendered_at.isoformat()),
    ],
    columns=["Field", "Recorded value"],
)
```

#| label: reporting-scope

display(

        "**MMC Watershed Data** retrieves rainfall observations from the City "
        "of Auburn LI-COR network and the City of Opelika THOR network, "
        "preserves the API responses as evidence, validates their structure, "

)

# Station and watershed location

The Moores Mill Creek (MMC) watershed is the land area where surface runoff
drains toward Moores Mill Creek. Its boundary defines the geographic area of
interest for this project. Figure 1 places the configured Auburn and Opelika
rainfall stations relative to that boundary: blue points are Auburn stations,
red points are Opelika stations, and the green polygon is the watershed.

Each station measures rainfall at one location. Stations inside and around the
watershed help show how rainfall varies across the area, but an individual
station value should not be interpreted as rainfall over the entire watershed.

```{python}
#| label: fig-station-map
#| fig-cap: "Auburn and Opelika rainfall stations relative to the Moores Mill Creek watershed boundary."
#| fig-alt: "Map showing the Moores Mill Creek watershed boundary and rainfall stations colored by city."
#| fig-width: 7
#| fig-height: 6
#| fig-pos: H

city_colors = {"Auburn": "#1f77b4", "Opelika": "#d62728"}
boundary_latitudes = [latitude for latitude, _longitude in watershed_boundary]
boundary_longitudes = [longitude for _latitude, longitude in watershed_boundary]
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7, 6))
ax.fill(
    boundary_longitudes,
    boundary_latitudes,
    color="#8fb996",
    alpha=0.22,
)
ax.plot(
    boundary_longitudes,
    boundary_latitudes,
    color="#2f6b3b",
    linewidth=2,
)
for city in ("Auburn", "Opelika"):
    city_points = [point for point in station_points if point.city == city]
    ax.scatter(
        [point.longitude for point in city_points],
        [point.latitude for point in city_points],
        color=city_colors[city],
        edgecolor="white",
        linewidth=0.7,
        s=55,
        zorder=3,
    )
    for point in city_points:
        ax.annotate(
            point.station_name,
            (point.longitude, point.latitude),
            xytext=(4, 4),
            textcoords="offset points",
            fontsize=7,
        )
ax.set_xlabel("Longitude")
ax.set_ylabel("Latitude")
ax.set_title("MMC watershed and rainfall station locations")
ax.set_aspect("equal", adjustable="datalim")
ax.grid(alpha=0.15)
ax.legend(
    handles=[
        Line2D([0], [0], color="#2f6b3b", linewidth=2, label="MMC watershed"),
        Line2D(
            [0],
            [0],
            marker="o",
            color="none",
            markerfacecolor=city_colors["Auburn"],
            markeredgecolor="white",
            markersize=7,
            label="Auburn station",
        ),
        Line2D(
            [0],
            [0],
            marker="o",
            color="none",
            markerfacecolor=city_colors["Opelika"],
            markeredgecolor="white",
            markersize=7,
            label="Opelika station",
        ),
    ],
    loc="best",
)
fig.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

# Data and method

The report selects one complete processed collection using the date range
encoded in MMC's station filenames. It always chooses the collection most
recently written under `data/processed/`, so its period follows the latest API
collection made with `mmc`. If no generated collection exists, the report uses
the bundled dataset under `reports/data/` so the repository PDF remains
reproducible offline.

All records are loaded through `mmc_watershed_data.reporting`, which calls the
project's typed `load_rainfall_records` function. The report does not recreate
Auburn epoch conversion, Opelika cumulative-counter conversion, Pydantic
validation, or API requests. Rainfall totals are sums of processed interval
`RainIn` values in inches. The processed CSVs already contain one `RainIn`
value per source observation at a nominal 10-minute cadence. The station
time-series figures plot those rows directly at their saved `Date_hour`
timestamps; the report does not resample or sum them into new time windows.

## Rainfall totals

Blue bars identify Auburn stations and red bars identify Opelika stations,
matching the city colors used by the dashboard. The legend makes that encoding
explicit.

```{python}
#| label: fig-station-totals
#| fig-cap: "Total processed interval rainfall by station for the selected reporting period."
#| fig-alt: "Horizontal bar chart of total rainfall by station, with Auburn in blue and Opelika in red."
#| fig-width: 7
#| fig-height: 4.8
#| fig-pos: H

plot_data = station_summary.sort_values("total_rain_in")
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7, 4.8))
bars = ax.barh(
    plot_data["station_name"],
    plot_data["total_rain_in"],
    color=[city_colors[city] for city in plot_data["city"]],
)
ax.bar_label(bars, fmt="%.2f", padding=3, fontsize=8)
ax.set_xlabel("Total processed interval rainfall (inches)")
ax.set_ylabel("Station")
ax.set_title(f"Station rainfall totals, {dataset.start_date} to {dataset.end_date}")
ax.legend(
    handles=[
        Patch(color=city_colors["Auburn"], label="Auburn"),
        Patch(color=city_colors["Opelika"], label="Opelika"),
    ],
    title="City",
    loc="lower right",
)
ax.grid(axis="x", alpha=0.2)
fig.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

## Rainfall at 10-minute intervals

Each panel below represents one station over the full selected period. Every
bar reports one `RainIn` value directly from the processed CSV; the shared
horizontal scale makes the timing of rainfall comparable across stations.

```{python}
#| label: fig-auburn-interval-rainfall
#| fig-cap: "Auburn processed rainfall observations at a nominal 10-minute cadence during the selected reporting period."
#| fig-alt: "Stacked time-series bar charts showing 10-minute rainfall for each represented Auburn station."
#| fig-width: 7
#| fig-height: 8
#| fig-pos: H

def plot_station_intervals(city: str) -> None:
    """Plot processed rainfall rows for each represented city station."""

    city_data = time_series_frame.loc[time_series_frame["city"] == city]
    station_names = sorted(city_data["station_name"].unique())
    if not station_names:
        display(Markdown(f"No processed {city} stations were available."))
        return

    fig, axes = plt.subplots(
        len(station_names),
        1,
        figsize=(7, max(2.2 * len(station_names), 3.2)),
        sharex=True,
        squeeze=False,
    )
    for ax, station_name in zip(axes[:, 0], station_names, strict=True):
        station_data = city_data.loc[city_data["station_name"] == station_name]
        wet_data = station_data.loc[station_data["rain_in"] > 0]
        ax.bar(
            wet_data["timestamp"],
            wet_data["rain_in"],
            width=10 / (24 * 60),
            color=city_colors[city],
            align="center",
        )
        ax.set_ylabel("Rain (in)")
        ax.set_title(station_name, loc="left", fontsize=9, fontweight="bold")
        ax.set_xlim(chart_start, chart_end)
        ax.grid(axis="y", alpha=0.2)

    axes[-1, 0].set_xlabel("Observation time (fixed UTC-6 local time)")
    axes[-1, 0].xaxis.set_major_locator(mdates.AutoDateLocator(minticks=4, maxticks=8))
    axes[-1, 0].xaxis.set_major_formatter(mdates.ConciseDateFormatter(
        axes[-1, 0].xaxis.get_major_locator()
    ))
    fig.suptitle(f"{city} rainfall by station", fontweight="bold")
    fig.tight_layout()
    plt.show()


plot_station_intervals("Auburn")
```

## Interpretation and limitations

```{python}
#| label: interpretation
#| output: asis

display(
    Markdown(
        f"The selected records show that **{winner['station_name']}** had the "
        f"largest accumulated interval total during **{period_label}**. The "
        f"comparison describes the observations available in the selected "
        f"collection; it does not estimate rainfall between stations or prove "
        f"that one part of the watershed received more rainfall everywhere. "
        f"Auburn and Opelika can have different source sampling behavior, and "
        f"station failures or empty responses reduce coverage."
    )
)
```

After collecting a period, the report automatically selects the most recently
written processed collection:

```bash
uv run mmc --start-date 2026-01-01 --end-date 2026-01-08
quarto render reports/mmc-rainfall-report.qmd --to pdf
```

The report source, inputs, PDF, metadata, and logs contain no API key or other
secret.
